description: Baseline performance thresholds. Keys are the benchmark_name values scripts/export_benchmark_jsonl.ps1 writes (Criterion ids). benchmark.yml prefixes package:: ; the checker strips that prefix. The old ids ecs_benchmarks/entity_spawn, ecs_benchmarks/entity_tick_empty, ecs_performance/stress_10k_entities, and input_benchmarks/full_input_set_processing are not rows the runner writes. entity_spawning and world_tick are the core_benchmarks ids.

policy.comment: Thresholds set from Week 2 baseline metrics + Week 3 optimizations

world_creation.description: ECS World creation on ubuntu-latest. The 25.8 ns laptop figure is not this runner. Three healthy aggregates on 2026-10-28 were 41.47, 42.62, and 42.87 ns. Cap is 1.5x the slowest of those.

entity_spawning.description: Spawn 100 entities (core_benchmarks). ubuntu-latest means from runs 40756735213 (30830.93 ns), 40742663481 (30805.26 ns), 40647488491 (17653.34 ns), and 40637628179 (30493.92 ns). Cap is 1.5x the slowest, rounded to 0.01 ns.

world_tick.description: One tick of 50 entities (core_benchmarks). ubuntu-latest means from the same four runs: 45.82, 48.39, 24.38, and 48.49 ns. Cap is 1.5x the slowest, rounded to 0.01 ns.

behavior_tree_20_nodes.description: Complex behavior tree on ubuntu-latest. The 253 ns baseline left max_allowed at 379.5, about 10 ns above the high cluster: 369.66 ns on run 40165571400 and 369.56 ns on run 40455623588. The same commit also measured 185.87 ns (run 40274704065). Cap is 1.5x 369.66 ns, the slower of those samples. warn_threshold is 1.25x.

raycast_ground_plane.description: Raycast vs a stepped ground plane on ubuntu-latest. The 44 ns cap measured a query pipeline that had not been stepped, so the ray missed. The bench now calls world.step() and asserts a hit. ubuntu-latest means: 194.61 ns (run 39532631733), 186.55, 173.12, 191.1, 184.9, 156. Cap is 1.5x the slowest. Empty-scene on the same runners stays near 13 ns, under its old cap.

raycast_batch_8_rays.description: Eight hitting raycasts on ubuntu-latest. The bench does not call world.step(). It calls query_pipeline.update so the boxes are in the broad phase, and the loop asserts hit_count >= 2. The 273 ns cap was eight misses. The cap is 1.5x 2309.9 ns from run 39532631733 (max_allowed 3464.85). Later ubuntu-latest means are higher and still under that cap: 2388.78 ns (run 40455623588), 2385.60 ns (run 40647488491), 2316.25 ns (run 40066299246). Windows and macOS do not run this workflow.
